name: Wyoming
tagline: From Beartooth Pass and the Bighorns to Oregon Trail ruts and red-desert backways.
intro: Wyoming's byways cross the Beartooth, Absaroka, Bighorn and Medicine Bow ranges, run up to the gates of Yellowstone and Grand Teton, and follow emigrant trails and old stock roads across the basins between. This chapter follows the Wyoming Scenic Byways and Backways Program of the Wyoming Department of Transportation, whose Transportation Commission adopts each route; WYDOT publishes no current list, so the roster comes from its 2009 program book and the Wyoming Office of Tourism's count of 21. The program has two tiers, paved byways for any car and backways on county and Forest Service roads, some of them gravel that turns impassable when wet, and every national forest and BLM route in the state is also a state member.

members.name: Chief Joseph Scenic Highway
members.blurb: WYO 296 runs 47 miles through the Absaroka Mountains to the Clarks Fork valley and the Beartooth Highway, crossing Sunlight Basin, where grizzlies sometimes feed near the road in spring, close to the Nez Perce route of 1877.

members.name: Beartooth Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 212 climbs from Red Lodge, Montana, onto the high Beartooth Plateau and crests at 10,947-foot Beartooth Pass, where snowbanks can linger into August, before dropping to Yellowstone's Northeast Entrance.

members.name: Buffalo Bill Cody Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 14/16/20 follows the North Fork of the Shoshone River up the Wapiti Valley for 27 miles to Yellowstone's East Entrance, passing Pahaska Teepee, Buffalo Bill's old hunting lodge.

members.name: Big Horn Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 14 crosses the Bighorns from Dayton over 9,033-foot Granite Pass, then switchbacks down Shell Canyon past Shell Falls, where the creek drops 120 feet beside a short nature trail, to the town of Shell.

members.name: Medicine Wheel Passage
members.blurb: US 14A runs 27 miles west from Burgess Junction past the Medicine Wheel on Medicine Mountain, a ring of limestone boulders some 80 feet across with 28 spokes, then down 10-percent grades toward Lovell.

members.name: Cloud Peak Skyway
members.blurb: US 16 crosses the southern Bighorns from Buffalo to Ten Sleep over 9,666-foot Powder River Pass, with a view of 13,167-foot Cloud Peak, then drops between the rock walls of Ten Sleep Canyon.

members.name: Wyoming Centennial Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 163-mile horseshoe from Dubois over Togwotee Pass on the Continental Divide, down past the Tetons through Jackson and Hoback Canyon to Pinedale, where the Museum of the Mountain Man keeps the fur-trade story.

members.name: Snowy Range Scenic Byway
members.blurb: WYO 130 crosses the Medicine Bow Mountains between Centennial and Saratoga, rising to 10,847 feet below 12,013-foot Medicine Bow Peak, past Mirror Lake and wind-bent krummholz spruce. Snow closes it from fall to late May.

members.name: Mirror Lake Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The Wyoming end of the Mirror Lake road follows WYO 150 south from Evanston through sagebrush flats and aspen toward the Uinta Mountains, the only major range in the lower states that runs east to west.

members.name: Flaming Gorge - Green River Basin Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A loop of high desert and red rock around Flaming Gorge Reservoir, south from Green River on WYO 530 and back north on US 191 to Rock Springs, starting near Expedition Island, where John Wesley Powell launched in 1869.

members.name: Bridger Valley Historic Byway
members.blurb: A short loop off I-80 through Lyman, Urie and Fort Bridger, where a replica of Jim Bridger's 1843 trading post stands at the old fort beside a restored tourist court from the Lincoln Highway years.

members.name: Wind River Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 20 runs north from Shoshoni past Boysen Reservoir into Wind River Canyon on the Wind River Indian Reservation, between walls 2,500 feet high with signs naming each rock layer, to the Wedding of the Waters near Thermopolis.

members.name: Oregon Trail Historic Byway
members.blurb: US 26 runs 57 miles up the North Platte valley from the Nebraska line through Torrington and Fort Laramie to Guernsey, where wagon wheels wore ruts into solid rock and emigrants carved their names in Register Cliff.

members.name: Battle Pass Scenic Byway
members.blurb: WYO 70 climbs west from Encampment over the Sierra Madre to the Continental Divide at 9,955-foot Battle Pass, past the ghost town site of Battle and a Battle Lake overlook where Thomas Edison vacationed in 1878.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Wyoming Black Hills Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 78-mile route on the Wyoming side of the Black Hills near Newcastle, where pine-dark hills rise from open grassland, with the ghost towns of Cambria and Tubb Town and the Anna Miller Museum nearby.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Star Valley Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 89 comes in from Idaho, climbs Salt Canyon to 7,610-foot Salt River Pass and runs down Star Valley through Afton and Thayne to Alpine, then follows the Snake River Canyon toward Hoback Junction.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: South Big Horn/Red Wall Scenic Backway
members.blurb: A 102-mile gravel horseshoe off US 20/26 west of Casper, up the old stock driveway across Fifty-Mile Flat to ponderosa pine and the long red escarpment of the Red Wall, with Hole-in-the-Wall a few miles north.

members.name: Red Gulch/Alkali Scenic Backway
members.blurb: Thirty-two miles of gravel through red Chugwater hills and hoodoos on the west slope of the Bighorns, from US 14 near Shell to Hyattville, past the Red Gulch Dinosaur Tracksite and its footprints in Jurassic stone.
members.note: Shown on the map as Red Gulch/Alkali National Back Country Byway.

members.name: Seminoe to Alcova Scenic Backway
members.blurb: County Road 351 leaves I-80 at Sinclair and runs 64 miles north to Alcova, past Seminoe Reservoir, over the steep Seminoe Mountains and across the Miracle Mile of the North Platte, a blue-ribbon trout water.

members.name: Big Spring Scenic Backway
members.blurb: A rough 68-mile road from Kemmerer to Cokeville into the Tunp Range of the Bridger National Forest, past old wagon ruts and an abandoned settler's cabin, with high clearance advised west of Kelley Guard Station.

members.name: Muddy Creek Historic Backway
members.blurb: Twenty-five miles of gravel from Fort Bridger to the ghost town of Piedmont and its charcoal kilns, by way of Muddy Creek, a camp for Mormon emigrants in 1847 and later a Pony Express station.
